questions.q: After administration, drugs are first rapidly distributed to:

options.t: Blood-rich organs: heart, liver, kidney, brain
options.e: Correct. Then to muscle, fat and skin with poor blood supply.
Wrong. Only specific drugs accumulate there.

questions.q: Which properties give a drug wide distribution into tissues?

options.t: Unionized, highly lipid soluble, low plasma protein binding
options.e: Correct. They pass easily to interstitial and cellular compartments.
Wrong. Stays in the vascular space.

questions.q: Iodide selectively accumulates in:
Tetracyclines accumulate in:

options.e: Correct. They bind calcium in bone and teeth.

questions.q: Chloroquine accumulates selectively in:
The redistribution phenomenon is:

options.t: Termination of action by moving the drug from the site of action to other tissues
options.e: Correct. The drug is still active but not producing action there.

questions.q: The classic example of redistribution is:

options.e: Correct. Ultrashort barbiturate moving from CNS to muscle and fat.

questions.q: Thiopental anaesthesia ends within 10-15 minutes mainly because of:

options.t: Redistribution from CNS to muscle and fat

questions.q: What happens after repeated injections of thiopental?

options.t: Storage sites saturate and action is prolonged
options.e: Correct. Termination then depends on metabolism and excretion.

questions.q: A drug bound to plasma proteins is:

options.t: Inactive, not metabolized and not excreted
options.e: Correct. It cannot diffuse out of the vascular space.
Wrong. Only the free drug does that.
Wrong. Bound drug is not metabolized.

questions.q: Plasma protein binding acts as a reservoir because:

options.t: Drug unbinds when the free concentration falls

questions.q: Sulfonamides displacing bilirubin from albumin can cause:

options.e: Correct. Increased free bilirubin causes bilirubin encephalopathy.

questions.q: In liver or renal disease with low plasma proteins, which drug dose should be reduced?

options.t: Highly protein-bound drugs such as warfarin
options.e: Correct. More free drug is available.

questions.q: For a drug with very high plasma protein binding such as diazoxide, which administration is needed?

options.e: Correct. To overcome binding and achieve effective free levels.

questions.q: Quinidine increases free digoxin by:

options.e: Wrong. The effect is the opposite.

options.t: Displacing it from plasma and tissue proteins and reducing its renal excretion
options.e: Correct. All three effects raise digoxin toxicity risk.

questions.q: Volume of distribution (Vd) equals:

options.t: Amount of drug in the body divided by plasma concentration
options.e: Correct. The apparent volume needed to contain the drug at plasma concentration.

questions.q: A high Vd indicates:

options.t: Low plasma concentration; drug distributed widely to tissues
options.e: Correct. Most of the drug is outside plasma.

questions.q: Which factors increase Vd?

options.t: Unionized, lipid soluble, low plasma protein binding, high tissue binding

questions.q: In digoxin toxicity, hemodialysis is not helpful because:

options.t: Digoxin is highly protein bound in plasma

options.e: Wrong. It has a high Vd.

options.t: High Vd means most drug is in tissues
options.e: Correct. Dialysis cannot remove tissue-bound drug.

questions.q: In aspirin toxicity, hemodialysis can remove most of the drug because aspirin has:

options.t: A low Vd, so it is concentrated in blood
options.e: Correct. It remains mainly in plasma.

questions.q: Drugs with high Vd show:

options.e: Correct. Tissues act as a reservoir.

questions.q: Steady state concentration is reached when:

options.t: Rate of elimination equals rate of administration
